sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The LPI Conflict Transformantion Programme in DRC in partnership with Congolese civil society organisations, contributed to the constructive involvement of conflict actors in the Great Lakes region in conflict transformation. Through this programme, LPI supported sustainable and nonviolent transformation of underlying and protracted local intra and inter-community conflicts at the grassroots level by supporting civil society organisations in their work on land conflicts and inclusion of all conflict actors in a participatory analysis. In addition, the programme contributed to the ability of key decision-makers to support long-term, nonviolent conflict transformation processes that address root causes of conflict. Finally, the DRC programme integrated the perspectives and needs of women into Participatory Action Research (PAR) processes and subsequent conflict transformation activities.
The programme has had a significant positive impact in Eastern DRC, and the participatory action research processes and conflict transformation structures are still relevant in the areas where they were launched. Some structures continue to exist in the communities where LPI and its partners were engaged, showing that LPI’s efforts to support ownership and sustainability has born fruit.
The project ended one year early due to weak financial management systems at the level of LPI and some of its local partners, and this naturally had an impact on results. However, regardless of the fact that one full year of activities were cut, the project still reports interesting results.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
